Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
This document explains how Aurora Bank handles complaints and supports customers who need additional help. Contact routes and service levels are listed in [Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels](12_glossary_contact_and_service_level.md).

Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility
5. Escalation and external review
If the customer is not satisfied with the final response, they may be able to refer the complaint to an ombudsman, financial services mediator, data protection authority, court, or regulator depending on complaint type and jurisdiction. The final response will include relevant escalation information where required.
Customers usually must complain to Aurora Bank before using an external dispute resolution body.

Account Opening, Eligibility & Customer Verification Policy
9. Customers who need support
Aurora Bank will make reasonable adjustments for customers who cannot complete standard onboarding because of disability, illness, digital exclusion, language barriers, domestic abuse, homelessness, displacement, or other vulnerability. Examples include branch appointments, interpreter support, alternative documents, large-print forms, and trusted-contact procedures.
Support options are described in [Complaints, Vulnerable Customers & Accessibility](10_complaints_vulnerable_customers_and_accessibility.md).

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
9. Arranged overdrafts
An arranged overdraft is intended as a short-term borrowing facility. It should not be used for long-term borrowing or regular living costs. Aurora Bank may review, reduce, suspend, or cancel an overdraft after notice or immediately where required for risk, fraud, legal, or account-conduct reasons.
Important overdraft rules:
- Interest is charged only on the used arranged overdraft balance.
- The overdraft is repayable on demand.
- Exceeding the limit may lead to declined payments and fees.
- An overdraft limit is not a promise that every payment will be honored.
- Savings accounts and youth accounts do not have overdrafts.

Current & Savings Accounts Terms
6. Overdraft basics
An arranged overdraft is a credit facility attached to a current account. It allows the balance to go below zero up to an approved limit. Arranged overdrafts are subject to credit assessment and are not guaranteed. Details are in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).
An unarranged overdraft occurs when the account goes below zero without approval or exceeds an arranged limit. Aurora Bank may refuse payments that would create or increase an unarranged overdraft. Fees and interest may apply as described in [Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange](06_fees_interest_and_exchange_rates.md).
Youth accounts, Basic Payment Accounts, savings accounts, and Fixed Term Deposits do not offer arranged overdrafts.

Fees, Interest & Foreign Exchange
5. Overdraft fees and interest
Arranged overdraft interest is calculated daily on the used arranged overdraft balance and charged monthly. The illustrative arranged overdraft rate is 13.90% annual nominal variable.
Aurora Bank does not charge a separate daily unarranged overdraft fee in this mock fee schedule. However, payments that exceed the available balance may be rejected and failed-payment fees may apply where permitted. If an unarranged negative balance occurs, debit interest may be charged and the customer must repay it immediately.
The bank may reduce or waive fees where financial difficulty is confirmed. Hardship support is described in [Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment](05_loans_overdrafts_and_credit_assessment.md).

Loans, Overdrafts & Credit Assessment
1. Lending products covered
Aurora Bank may offer the following consumer credit products:
| Product | Typical purpose | Repayment style | Security |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal loan | Car, home improvement, education, debt consolidation, major purchase | Fixed monthly instalments | Usually unsecured |
| Arranged overdraft | Short-term cash-flow buffer linked to current account | Repayable on demand; interest charged on used balance | Unsecured |
| Credit card | Flexible purchases and short-term borrowing | Minimum monthly payment; revolving balance | Unsecured |
| Mortgage referral or home loan | Property purchase or refinancing | Monthly instalments over long term | Secured on property |
| Green home improvement loan | Energy-efficiency upgrades | Fixed instalments | Usually unsecured, invoices may be required |
Product availability depends on jurisdiction, customer profile, and regulatory permission.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
3. Cutoff times
Cutoff times are shown in Central European Time unless otherwise stated. They can change during public holidays, system maintenance, or payment-scheme disruption.
| Payment type | Standard cutoff | Execution expectation |
|---|---:|---|
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in online banking | 15:30 on a business day | Sent same business day; usually credited by beneficiary bank by next business day. |
| SEPA Credit Transfer submitted in branch | 14:00 on a business day | Sent same business day if accepted before cutoff. |
| SEPA Instant Credit Transfer | 24/7 where available | Usually within seconds; may fall back or be declined if unavailable. |
| Internal transfer between own Aurora accounts | 24/7 | Usually immediate. |
| Internal transfer to another Aurora customer | 22:00 daily | Usually same day after security checks. |
| International wire in EUR | 13:00 on a business day | Usually 1-2 business days, depending on route. |
| International wire in non-EUR currency | 11:30 on a business day | Usually 2-5 business days, depending on currency and intermediaries. |
| Standing order creation or amendment | 18:00 the business day before due date | Changes after cutoff may apply to the next cycle only. |
| Direct debit cancellation | 18:00 the business day before collection date | Later cancellation may not stop the payment. |
Cutoff times are not promises that the beneficiary will receive funds at a specific hour. Intermediary banks, receiving banks, screening, incorrect details, and payment-system availability may affect timing.

Payments, Transfers & Cutoff Times
6. Payment authentication
Payments may require strong customer authentication. Authentication can include a password, app confirmation, biometric confirmation, one-time passcode, hardware token, or call-back verification. Aurora Bank will never ask a customer to disclose a full password, full card PIN, or remote-access code.
Additional security checks may delay a payment. Aurora Bank may hold or reject a payment if fraud, sanctions, money laundering, scam, account takeover, or unusual activity indicators are present.

Glossary, Contact Channels & Service Levels
3. Definitions
Cutoff time
The latest time on a business day when Aurora Bank normally accepts a payment instruction for same-day processing.
